subject: DevSolutions migration: cost, packaging, and parity tradeoffs
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@devsolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial econ comparison and draft packaging — Redwood vs CloudRun

Hi Lina,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a concise econ workbook comparing Redwood with your incumbent (CloudRun) across the key vectors you called out: per-token runtime units, reserved capacity vs burst, caching assumptions, and expected egress. I pulled conservative latency and batching assumptions to avoid surprise.

Two quick notes up front:
- We can match the incumbent's published seat-level discount if you commit to a 12-month reserved pool (we outline the tiers in the attached sheet).
- For the first 90 days we recommend a migration cushion: 20% credits on your first-month inference spend for ops friction / integration validation.

Attachments: redwood-vs-cloudrun-econ.xlsx (workbook), redwood-migration-checklist.pdf

Next steps: can you confirm the current average monthly token consumption you see (rough order of magnitude is fine)? That will let us run the exact match scenario and show net TCO over 12 and 24 months.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@devsolutions.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-16T14:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial econ comparison and draft packaging — Redwood vs CloudRun

Naomi — thanks for the workbook. A few pricing scenarios we can use depending on the procurement ask:

1) Straight match (12-month reserved): match incumbent list-per-token and offer 6 weeks of technical credits (covers migration runbooks).
2) Match + onboarding cushion (12-month reserved + 90-day credit): match price and add 20% first-month credit as you suggested — sweet spot for revenue ops.
3) Lower commitment (6-month reserved): competitive per-token but with a small fidelity uplift fee (~5%) on burst usage; helpful if they are uncomfortable with longer-term locks.

Also included in the econ tab is a sensitivity where we assume 25% KV-cache hit vs 10% (their ops team can likely increase that with minor prompt changes). If Lina confirms avg tokens, I can produce an apples-to-apples blended unit price and an executed quote we can push through the portal.

Attachments referenced: updated econ tab within redwood-vs-cloudrun-econ.xlsx

—Marissa
Marissa Cole, Pricing & Deals
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

---
From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@devsolutions.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-17T10:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial econ comparison and draft packaging — Redwood vs CloudRun

Lina — quick tech note to pair with Marissa's pricing scenarios:

- Onboarding delta: CloudRun currently uses a mostly single-node KV cache strategy. To get to our higher cache hit rates you'd likely update a small set of prompt templates and deploy lightweight caching agents (we'll provide the runbook). I estimate ~3 engineer-weeks for the initial migration to reach 60% parity in latency under normal load.
- Egress/throughput: if you have burst spikes > 120 RPS, reserve pool sizing matters. We can architect hybrid: baseline reserved capacity sized for 95th percentile and burst to hosted for spikes.
- Data residency / audit: we can stand up a private deployment (VPC) in your cloud if compliance requires it — pricing differs, but we'll mark that as optional in the workbook.

I'll loop into the migration checklist and flag any ops risk items. Happy to run a short technical workshop with your infra team next week.

Connor Obrien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai

---
From: Lina Park <lina.park@devsolutions.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Whittaker <ewhittaker@devsolutions.com>, procurement@devsolutions.com
Date: 2028-07-19T08:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial econ comparison and draft packaging — Redwood vs CloudRun

Hi Naomi / Marissa / Connor,

Thanks — that level of detail is helpful. A few items from procurement/eng that will determine the path:

1) Baseline volume: our platform currently consumes ~2.3B tokens/month (90th pctl over last 90 days).
2) Incumbent concessions: CloudRun offered an effective blended price of $0.0009 per token after tiering and an onboarding credit of ~$80k.
3) Compliance: we need SOC 2 evidence and an option for private VPC deployment in us-west-2.
4) Contract cadence: our finance team prefers quarterly invoicing for the first year.

For us to compare apples-to-apples, can you produce: i) executed quote showing the effective blended per-token for 12- and 24-month terms, ii) a breakdown of one-time onboarding credits vs recurring unit price, iii) a redline-friendly SOW that lists the 3 engineer-weeks you mentioned? Also please include the SOC2 link.

We aim to present an evaluation to the execs on 2028-07-26.

Regards,
Lina Park
Director, Platform Engineering
DevSolutions Inc

---
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@devsolutions.com>, procurement@devsolutions.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial econ comparison and draft packaging — Redwood vs CloudRun

Lina — appreciated, and great context. Next steps from our side:

- Marissa will publish two executed-quote PDFs (12m & 24m) with a clear effective blended per-token and a line-item showing the 90-day onboarding credit. Expect those by EOD 2028-07-20.
- I will attach SOC 2 link and a draft SOW that scopes the 3 engineer-weeks and the migration checklist items.
- Connor and I can host a 45-minute technical Q&A with your infra leads on 2028-07-24; let us know a time window.
- Regarding the finance cadence: our billing team can do quarterly invoices for the first year (we'll surface that in the quote).

I'll follow up once the docs are uploaded; if it speeds things up, is procurement comfortable with a non-binding Letter of Intent while legal completes the SOW?

Best,
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
